behaviour.room_temperature: Very high stiffness; room-temperature ductility can be limited by processing and microstructure.
behaviour.1000C: Substantial strength retention compared with conventional engineering metals; oxidation in air becomes a major constraint.
behaviour.1500C: High-temperature capability remains strong in controlled atmospheres, but recrystallisation and creep become increasingly important.
behaviour.2000C_plus: Specialist high-temperature/vacuum/inert applications; property data must be grade- and process-specific.

behaviour.room_temperature: Generally improved ductility/workability relative to susceptible pure-tungsten conditions.
behaviour.1000C: High-temperature mechanical performance remains relevant for instrumentation and specialist components.
behaviour.1500C: Grade-specific strength, creep and recrystallisation evidence required.
behaviour.2000C_plus: Specialist applications only; environment and grain stability are critical.

behaviour.room_temperature: Ductile binder phase gives substantially different behaviour from monolithic tungsten.
behaviour.500C: Strength and ductility become increasingly grade-dependent.
behaviour.1000C: Binder phase and microstructural stability govern performance; creep and phase stability require evidence.
behaviour.1500C: Generally unsuitable for many structural uses without highly specific grade/environment evidence.

behaviour.room_temperature: Extremely high hardness and compressive capability; fracture and edge chipping can govern.
behaviour.500C: Hardness and strength reduce with temperature; binder phase becomes increasingly important.
behaviour.800C: Hot hardness and oxidation/phase stability become application-critical.
behaviour.1000C_plus: Specialist high-temperature use requires grade-specific evidence; conventional room-temperature properties are not transferable.

behaviour.room_temperature: High conductivity combined with high stiffness/density.
behaviour.300C: Copper phase increasingly influences thermal and mechanical response.
behaviour.600C: Thermal mismatch and copper softening can dominate local performance.
behaviour.1000C_plus: Generally not a conventional structural high-temperature material; use requires composition-specific evidence.

behaviour.1000C: Improved resistance to deformation/recrystallisation relative to some unalloyed conditions.
behaviour.2000C_plus: Specialist electrode/furnace applications require source-specific evidence.
